abstract: Tepary bean (Phaseolus acutifolius A. Gray) is an arid-adapted legume, whose drought resilience is widely reported but poorly resolved genetically. Here we resequenced 363 wild, weedy, cultivated and breeding accessions and recovered 6.9 million single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). We phenotyped 282 of the accessions for growth, evapotranspiration and photosynthesis over 14 days at 60% or 10% soil water-holding capacity. Cultivated and breeding lines grew roughly twice as fast as wild accessions, and the proportional reduction in growth under drought did not differ between these germplasm classes. Evapotranspiration separated the classes under full irrigation, but converged under drought, making it the most plastic trait we measured. Canopy density predicted how much water a plant used, but not how well it tolerated losing it. Association mapping across 104 rank-normalized measurements yielded 113 significant SNPs at 46 positions, which resolved to three drought and six control loci. Three drought loci corresponded to 98 of the 113 SNPs, with the largest one localized on chromosome 8. This locus separates wild from cultivated accessions, and resolves to no gene. Three of the eight remaining loci carry candidates whose interval, expression under drought and published mechanism agree: a cytokinin oxidase, a CIPK1-clade kinase and the antenna subunit LHCB5. The most structure-independent locus localizes to 26 kb but implicates genes with no published role in water relations. Growth under drought and control conditions therefore rest on separate genetic bases, and the variation with the largest effect under deficit lies in haplotypes affected by domestication.
